There's a variety of\h\h YOLO architectures and model sizes. YOLO11 is the\h latest architecture and has the best performance,\h\h but YOLOv8 and YOLOv5 are more mature and have\h broader support on hardware platforms. Model sizes\h\h range from nano to extra large. I made a quick\h YouTube video comparing YOLO model performance\h\h on a Raspberry Pi 5 and a laptop equipped with an\h RTX 4050 GPU. If your data set has less than 200 images,\h\h a good starting point is 60 epochs. If\h your data set has more than 200 images,\h\h a good starting point is 40 epochs. Resolution is\h another parameter we can tweak, but generally it's\h\h safe to use the default resolution of 640x 640.\h However, if you want your model to run faster or\h\h if you know you'll be working with low resolution\h images, try using a lower resolution like 480x480.
